decisions.statement: A seat is read from the newest commit that wrote its page.
A seat's moment is the time of the commit that wrote that seat.
Values come back under the key names the old page had.
A body that will not load leaves that seat out of the answer.
A reading of a root's history is held only while that history has not moved.
A seat page removed from akasha is in no index.
Git history is walked by the path a seat page had rather than by the seat page type.
History is walked over the folder the seats sit in now and every folder they sat in before.
A seat is named in history by the file its page is rather than by that file's folder.
A seat page taken away holds nothing in history.
A seat page moved is taken away at the path it left.
Where more than one path could answer a seat's name, the newest path answers.
A root's history has moved where the commit that root is on has changed.

definition: what a seat last said, read back out of git after its page in akasha is gone
